props.title: Go
props.initialSlug: Three wild tales collide on one Christmas Eve

sections.content: Go (1999) revolutionized the multi-perspective crime comedy by splitting one wild night into three interconnected stories. Director Doug Liman crafted a pulsing, neon-drenched LA odyssey that feels like Pulp Fiction (1994) on ecstasy. The film launched breakout performances from Sarah Polley and Timothy Olyphant while perfectly capturing the underground rave culture of the late 90s. Its innovative structure influenced later films like 21 Grams (2003) and Babel (2006), proving that fractured narratives could deliver both style and substance.

sections.content: The late 90s saw an explosion of youth-driven crime films trying to capture Pulp Fiction's magic. Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead (1995) and 2 Days in the Valley (1996) attempted similar multi-character criminal webs, but Go stood out by focusing on young protagonists far outside the traditional mobster milieu. The film's pounding electronic soundtrack and kinetic editing created a distinct visual language that influenced later films like Snatch (2000) and Layer Cake (2004).

What sets Go apart is how it uses its structure to explore consequences rather than just being clever. Each segment reveals new layers of meaning in scenes we've already witnessed, similar to Jackie Brown (1997) and Out of Sight (1998). The film maintains incredible momentum while still developing its large ensemble cast, something later attempted by films like Crash (2004) and Traffic (2000) but rarely with such energetic precision. sections.content: Go's influence can be seen in how modern crime films handle parallel narratives and youth culture. Films like Spring Breakers (2012) and Good Time (2017) share its neon-soaked aesthetic and propulsive energy, while Brick (2005) similarly drops young protagonists into dangerous criminal situations. The film's DNA is particularly visible in Edgar Wright's work, especially Baby Driver (2017), which shares its mix of music, action, and youthful energy.
